findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no disinfectant available for bodily fluid clean up. Obtain bleach or another disinfectant by 5/26/26 to ensure disinfectant is available to minimize the spread or contamination of food, food contact surfaces, employees, or consumers by vomit or fecal matter.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One employee who was present did not have a Food Handler's certificate available during today's inspection. All employees handling food must be certified as either a food handler, or certified food protection manager. Obtain necessary paperwork to be made available by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There was a case of soda and a box of single service articles observed to be stored on the floor. Discussed this with the PIC and recommended putting a pallet or milk crate under these items. Ensure that all single service articles and food is stored at least six inches off of the ground.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned     EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: There was a plastic bag observed to be in the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing. CORRECTED- The bag was removed and the staff was educated. 

 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: There are single service articles that are observed to be stored with the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are inverted to protect the food contact surface from any contamination. 

(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.
